pages.lesson:
LESSON: GUIDED READING: FLUENCY

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Reading
Topic 2.6: Guided Reading: Fluency

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Guided Reading: Fluency. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why are greetings important?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read greetings and introduction phrases correctly for information
2. appreciate the value of introductions and greetings in maintaining relationships

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GUIDED READING: FLUENCY
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Guided Reading: Fluency helps you succeed in ARABIC LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GUIDED READING: FLUENCY
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Read greetings and introduction phrases correctly for information

What this means
In this part you learn to read greetings and introduction phrases correctly for information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read greetings and introduction phrases correctly for information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Reading: Fluency”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read greetings and introduction phrases correctly for information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate the value of introductions and greetings in maintaining relationships

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the value of introductions and greetings in maintaining relationships. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the value of introductions and greetings in maintaining relationships.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided Reading: Fluency to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the value of introductions and greetings in maintaining relationships. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Guided Reading: Fluency is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Reading: Fluency”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: read greetings and introduction phrases correctly for information)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided Reading: Fluency to a partner. (skill: appreciate the value of introductions and greetings in maintaining relationships)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Guided Reading: Fluency to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: read greetings and introduction phrases correctly for information.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the value of introductions and greetings in maintaining relationships.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Guided Reading: Fluency from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Guided Reading: Fluency: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Guided Reading: Fluency?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why are greetings important?
2. How can one ensure that they speak Arabic fluently?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Guided Reading: Fluency means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: read greetings and introduction phrases correctly for information.
5. Be able to: appreciate the value of introductions and greetings in maintaining relationships.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
